formationLoss.note: Fraction of a targeted formation lost per strike. A division of 15,000 at 1973 density (29-36 men/km2, Attrition Fig. 14, https://dupuyinstitute.org/2016/11/12/what-is-the-relationship-between-rate-of-fire-and-military-effectiveness/) spreads over ~420-520 km2. Glasstone and Dolan Table 12.09: Hiroshima casualties over a 'vulnerable area' of 9.36 sq mi (24 km2), Nagasaki 7.01 sq mi (18 km2) (https://archive.org/details/DTIC_ADA087568). One ~20 kt weapon -> 18-24 km2 / 420-520 km2 = 3.5-6%; 100-300 kt (area scales W^2/3, x2.9-6) -> 10-35%; first use targets the densest concentration, so mid 0.15.

cityLoss.note: Glasstone and Dolan Table 12.09: Hiroshima killed 68,000 of 256,300 (27%) and injured 76,000; Nagasaki killed 38,000 of 173,800 (22%) and injured 21,000. Killed fraction 0.22-0.27; mid 0.3 for modern yields; high 0.6 for a 100-300 kt weapon on a city core (vulnerable area x2.9-6 by W^2/3 scaling).

escalationThreshold.note: Share of own starting theater territory lost before first use. Deliberately simple escalation ladder; no empirical basis exists (no nuclear use since 1945). Educated guess.
